description:
MEDIUM AND VOCABULARY. Flat vector shapes on a near-black, untextured ground. There is no line work, no stroke, no texture, no gradient — everything is a filled shape with alpha, and where shapes overlap the alpha stacks into visible flat bands. Two element families and only two. (1) Circles: soft olive/sage/moss discs, semi-transparent, stacked into a short vertical column of roughly two to six that overlap into a lumpy chain, like a caterpillar or a stack of stones. Some discs sit behind at a much darker value and read as shadow-discs rather than as objects. (2) Triangles: sharp isoceles wedges in bone/cream and, behind them, a darker charcoal set, arrayed radially around the disc column with their points outward, so the column looks quilled, thorned, or serrated.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Nothing literal. The recurring read is a seed pod, burr, or thistle head — a soft vertical body with spines coming off it. In the seeds where the triangles are small it reads botanical/organic, a bud with thorns. In the seeds where the triangles are huge it stops being organic and reads as a torn-paper splat, a starburst, or a circular sawblade with a green bearing in the middle. In one seed it reads as nothing but a pile of mossy blobs.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. Black ground; the same green; the same cream; a single centred subject with margin around it; the same two shape primitives; the same construction logic of column-plus-radial-spines. Nobody is doing anything the others are not made of.

HOW THEY DIFFER — essentially along ONE axis, the size and count of the triangles relative to the discs. At one extreme, 10801 has NO triangles at all: a big dark-olive blob stack, nothing else, running off the bottom of its tile. Near it, 9548 and 9190 are small, timid, low-contrast — two or three dim green discs and a sliver of cream. In the middle, 9011, 9369, 10264 and 9727 are balanced: a legible green column with a fringe of small-to-medium spikes, which is the most convincing version of the idea. At the far extreme, 9906, 10443, 10622 and 10980 invert the figure entirely — the triangles grow so large and overlap so heavily that they merge into a nearly solid cream field occupying most of the tile, and the green discs collapse to a small kernel at its centre. 10085 is its own case: three or four large cream triangles all pointing the same way (right) rather than radially, so it reads as a chevron or arrowhead rather than a burr. Overall scale also varies very widely, from 9548 occupying maybe a fifth of its tile to 9906 and 10801 overflowing theirs.

FRAME. The subject floats centred with dead margin — the 512px single has empty black on all four sides and roughly half the canvas is unused. Several tiles do the opposite and are cut by their own bounds: 9011's top spike is sliced off the top edge, 9906 is cut at top and bottom, 10443 and 10980 at the bottom, 10622 at bottom and left, and 10801's blob stack is cut off flat at the bottom. So the frame is either ignored or collided with, rarely composed against.

PALETTE. Extremely narrow and deliberately so: one green hue family, one bone/cream, one charcoal grey, on near-black. No third hue appears anywhere in twelve seeds. It is effectively monochrome-plus-one. The cream against black is the only strong contrast in the work; the green against black is mid-contrast; the dark backing discs against black are nearly invisible, which is why the quiet seeds (9548, 9190) go faint.

STATES. Comparing 9011, 9190, 9369 and 9548 across neutral / stress / recovery, the change is consistent in direction. STRESS: the spikes lose count and lose brightness — they turn grey and blunt, several disappear, and the surviving ones are broader, fewer wedges; the discs flatten toward each other in value so the object looks duller and more uniform. RECOVERY: the discs grow noticeably larger and more opaque, and the spikes come back brighter, whiter, more numerous and longer — 9011 and 9369 in recovery are visibly furrier and more brilliant than in neutral. NEUTRAL sits between. So the axis being modulated is spine population and brightness plus disc scale. It is one continuous axis, not three distinct characters — stress is a de-tuned neutral rather than a different condition.

AT 120px. The archetypes survive: you can still tell a spiky green column from a cream splat from a bare blob. But within-type resolution collapses. The four cream-dominant seeds (9906, 10443, 10622, 10980) become one repeated shape — a pale ragged mass with a green dot in it — and I could not reliably tell them apart. 9011, 9369 and 10264 also converge on one another. 9548 nearly vanishes: dim green on black with no cream to carry it. 10801 and 10085 are the two that stay individual at browse size. On the state sheet at 120, the change is clearly visible on 9011 and 9369 (the recovery burr reads as spikier and brighter), marginal on 9190, and effectively invisible on 9548 — its three states read as the same picture.

IDENTITY ACROSS STATES. Strong. Disc count, disc positions, silhouette and overall placement are preserved across all three states for every seed shown; nothing is replaced or re-rolled. A token stays itself.

ARTIFACTS. Hard flat cuts where shapes meet the tile boundary (listed above). Heavy alpha banding where triangles overlap, producing stepped grey facets that read as accidental rather than drawn — most visible in 9727, 10443 and 10980 where charcoal triangles sit under cream ones. In 9906 and 10622 the cream mass has swallowed its own internal structure, so the individual triangles are only readable at the silhouette edge. No stroke anywhere, so shapes have no drawn edge; small triangles at 120px lose their points entirely.
